conclusion: The Erdos-Turan factor 2 per prime cannot be improved to (2-delta) by joint or reordered prime processing: the architecture reduces entirely to c(A), the largest subset whose pairwise sums are powers of 2, which satisfies c(A) in {1,2} and is defined order-blind, so the selection lemma with phi(k)=(2-delta)^k is logically equivalent to the target bound g(k) <= 2(2-delta)^k rather than a refinement of the 1934 bookkeeping. Two defects in the standard sketch of the halving step were found and witnessed exactly: the per-prime halving |B'| >= |B|/2 is false, and the assembled c(A) >= n/2^s is false without primitivity.
confidence: The two defect witnesses are exact integer arithmetic, re-verified by independent trial division, and can be checked by hand in a minute; lean on them fully. The order-blindness barrier is a proof and I would lean on it, with the stated scope: it bounds what the Erdos-Turan architecture can prove, not what is true, so it says nothing against an S-unit-equation proof. The exhaustive sweep (104,183 admissible sets) is bounded-box evidence only and is not a proof of the repaired lemma.
